news.title: 《Candy Crush》以《光环》、《辐射》和《末日》联动作品（包括混音音乐）庆祝 Xbox 25 周年
news.summary: 2026 is the 25th anniversary of Xbox, and it's been a tough year for the brand with mass layoffs, studio closu

content.v: 2026 is the 25th anniversary of Xbox, and it's been a tough year for the brand with mass layoffs, studio closures/divestitures, and game cancellations. But the celebrations are still going ahead, including an event from the Xbox-owned Candy Crush mobile game juggernaut.

Announced today, Candy Crush Saga is marking the Xbox anniversary with a "Game On" season that brings items and elements from Halo, Fallout, Sea of Thieves, Forza, Doom, Banjo-Kazooie, Crash Bandicoot, and Spyro into the game through a virtual pin-collection event. Additionally, the popular and recognizable music from some of those games is coming to Candy Crush in "unmistakable Candy style," developer King said.
https://www.gamespot.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/11/XboxPins.png?w=636

The Game On event runs now through December 6. Players earn the themed pins, including Master Chief's iconic helmet, by progressing through Candy Crush's various levels throughout the season. The pins are being released physically, too, and people can enter a contest at the Candy Crush website for a chance to win.
In terms of the updated music, Candy Crush Saga is adding "Candyfied" versions of music from Halo, Fallout, Sea of Thieves, Forza, Doom, and Banjo-Kazooie.

You can check out a neat behind-the-scenes video below to see how composer Federico Truzzi worked with the developers at King to remix the songs with a Candy Crush flavor. The music was recorded by the German Film Orchestra Babelsberg and the Bulgarische Orthodoxe Chor Berlin e.V. choir.

In other Xbox anniversary news, Xbox CEO Asha Sharma released a statement marking the milestone, and referencing how the future of gaming could be focused on AI and vibe-coding . Microsoft also released a new hub called Xbox Playback where you can see your biggest Xbox accomplishments over the past quarter-century.

news.title: 一半工作室被解雇后，新的《毁灭战士》游戏似乎以最奇怪的方式宣布
news.summary: Xbox CEO Asha Sharma has announced that id Software is officially working on a new game, believed to be anothe

content.v: Xbox CEO Asha Sharma has announced that id Software is officially working on a new game, believed to be another Doom title. This is happening after Sharma oversaw id Software losing half of its staff to layoffs that were part of the Xbox "reset."

Id Software replied to Sharma's post on Twitter to provide a few more details on the new game, which the team didn't say was a Doom game, but everyone suspects it will be. The studio said it's "incredibly excited" about the new game, which is in the works at id's studios in Texas and Frankfurt. Hugo Martin, an id Software veteran, is directing the game--don't expect to see or hear about it soon, though.
"It'll be some time before we're ready to share more but we can't wait for you to see what we're working on," the developer said.
https://www.gamespot.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/11/DoomGame_809f5f.jpg?w=636
Reporter Tom Warren said in July that id Software was in the "early stages" of developing a new Doom game, so this news today isn't totally surprising.

Sharma cut staff at id Software (and numerous other Xbox studios around the world) earlier this year as part of a "reset" of the Xbox business. Marty Stratton of id Software recently said the studio is "doing great," despite the mass layoffs.
Id Software's latest game was 2025's Doom: The Dark Ages. The game's newest update is coming on November 16, adding the new wave-based Slaughter mode .

news.title: 《瓦尔海姆》即将推出漫画系列，看起来很糟糕
news.summary: Valheim is expanding beyond video games once again, this time with an official comic book series featuring an

content.v: https://assets-prd.ignimgs.com/2026/11/12/valheim-comicbookcoverart1-1794514240051.jpg
Valheim is expanding beyond video games once again, this time with an official comic book series featuring an impressive lineup of talent from Marvel, DC, television, and animation.

Developer Iron Gate Studio has teamed up with GUNGNIR Books and MOOD Publishing to bring its Viking survival game to comics, with the first release planned for the first quarter of 2027. The multi-issue series will feature original stories set in the world of Valheim, rather than simply retelling the events of the game.

The writing team certainly has a pretty impressive portfolio that bodes well for the series. It includes Steve Orlando (Wonder Woman, Avengers), Deric A. Hughes and Ben Raab (Quantum Leap), J. Holtham (The Handmaid's Tale, Supergirl), Brea Grant (12 Hour Shift), Tim Sheridan (Masters of the Universe), and Olan Rogers (Final Space). They're joined by TD Orel, Chris Klian, Andrew Sanders, and GUNGNIR Books founder Matthew Medney.

On the art side, Scott Oakley, Vanessa Del Rey, Lucas Pereira, and Mario Del Pennino are among the confirmed artists, with Mohamad Samah overseeing production design. More talent is expected to be announced.

According to the announcement, the series will explore the mythology of Valheim's mysterious tenth Norse realm, introducing new adventures and perspectives on its gods, monsters, and dangerous environments. Expect plenty of exploration, survival, and presumably some very unfortunate encounters with the local wildlife.

“Valheim is one of those rare worlds that feels like it existed long before we ever discovered it. There are gods, monsters, entire civilizations, and a mythology so rich that the stories we can tell feel almost endless," said Matthew Medney from GUNGNIR Books. "For us, the opportunity to work alongside Iron Gate and MOOD Publishing to bring this universe into comics is extraordinary. And we've assembled an absolute army of creative talent to do it. We're not interested in simply retelling what millions of players have already experienced. We want to explore the legends that haven't been told, the corners of this world that haven't been seen, and create something that feels worthy of the incredible universe Iron Gate built. This is Valheim, and we're going to make it epic."

The comic marks another expansion for Valheim , which has now sold more than 17 million copies worldwide since launching into Steam Early Access in February 2021. The game has already made the jump to tabletop gaming with Valheim: The Board Game, also developed in partnership with MOOD Publishing.

For now, there's no specific release date beyond Q1 2027, and details about individual issues, collectible editions, and how fans can get involved are still to come. In the meantime, Valheim players can look forward to exploring the tenth realm without having to worry about keeping their food buffs topped up. Which, frankly, sounds rather nice.

news.title: 《神鬼寓言》放弃了四分钟的新游戏玩法
news.summary: Four minutes of new Fable gameplay has been released by Xbox, showing off more of the game's combat.

content.v: https://assets-prd.ignimgs.com/2026/01/23/fable-thefirstpreview-blogroll-1769205292794.jpg
Four minutes of new Fable gameplay has been released by Xbox, showing off more of the game's combat.

The footage was released personally by Xbox CEO Asha Sharma as part of a larger celebration for the company's 25th anniversary. The gameplay shows off a bunch of combat, highlighting not only standard swordplay, but also ranged attacks and unique moves that can be performed using magic. The gameplay was captured on PC using ultra graphics settings and concludes with the protagonist stumbling upon an incredibly sinister-looking tomb or coffin.

Fable was, of course, meant to have been released this fall . However, Xbox made the smart decision to delay the game to February . Although the team says the delay wasn't done specifically in an effort to avoid GTA 6 , it was likely a nice benefit. Microsoft still had plenty of releases this autumn thanks to Modern Warfare 4 and Gears of War: E-Day, so it was wise to give Fable some more room to breathe. The game was announced all the way back in 2020, but has been in some form of development at Playground Games for nearly a decade.

Forza Horizon studio Playground Games is leading the charge on the title, though it has recruited a bunch of talent from around the industry so that it is well-equipped to build an RPG. Fable is one of the most anticipated games on Xbox's slate, partially because it's one of the most beloved RPG franchises out there, and Microsoft is looking for a big win in the AAA space outside of shooters.

Fable is also coming to PS5, as it had been previously announced for the platform. It'll be interesting to see what happens if the game performs well on the platform. Xbox is trying to lean more into exclusivity, but it unfortunately didn't seem to pay off for Gears of War: E-Day . Here's hoping Fable is worth the wait and pays off on Microsoft's investments.
Fable will release on Xbox Series X|S, PS5, and PC on February 23.

news.title: Take-Two 老板表示，游戏将永远留下物理足迹，但它会“非常小”
news.summary: It's no secret that the market for physical video games is drying up, but don't expect physical media for gami

content.v: It's no secret that the market for physical video games is drying up, but don't expect physical media for gaming to go away entirely anytime soon, or ever, according to Take-Two's Strauss Zelnick.

He told The Game Business that it "may not be the end" for physical media entirely in games, even with Sony killing off PlayStation discs in 2028 . He said there will "always be some physical business" for gaming, but it will be a "very small part of the business."
https://www.gamespot.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/11/Jason_and_Lucia_17_1e1bc0.jpg?w=636
He likened the scale of it to the vinyl business for recorded music. Most people might stream music today, but the market for vinyl is still there--and it's growing.

For Take-Two, however, Zelnick said its business today is 98% digital. Going all-digital has a lot of benefits for publishers, but it's mainly about making more money. For GTA 6, the most highly anticipated game release ever, Rockstar is not offering the game on a disc, but the game will appear in stores via a code-in-a-box version.

GTA 6's $400 collector's edition comes with a range of physical goods (but not the game), and Rockstar is also releasing GTA 6's score on CD and vinyl , but the game itself remains a digital-only experience.
GTA 6 launches on November 19 for PS5 and Xbox Series X|S. A PC edition and online multiplayer are both rumored to launch in 2027 .

news.title: “也许我们已经走得太远了”——《时之笛》重制版制作人透露，游戏的重死原本应该更可怕
news.summary: Producer Hidemaro Fujibayashi explained why the development team behind the Ocarina of Time Remake toned down

content.v: https://assets-prd.ignimgs.com/2026/11/12/oot-remake-redeads-were-supposed-to-be-scarier-1794513289206.jpg
Producer Hidemaro Fujibayashi explained why the development team behind the Ocarina of Time Remake toned down the ReDeads to make them less scary.

If you grew up playing the original Ocarina of Time on the Nintendo 64, you were probably traumatized by some of the game’s famously frightening enemies like the Gibdos, ReDeads, and Dead Hands. These last two were particularly terrifying for young players at the time — partially because we were still kids, and partially due to the N64’s graphical limitations that forced our minds to fill in the visual gaps in the monsters’ designs.

These enemies were a particular talking point when the Remake was first announced. Some players were doubtful that this new game could truly capture the terror of the original monsters, since a) it’s a game that’s also supposed to appeal to children and b) the updated graphics of modern Nintendo consoles don’t necessarily allow for the ‘fear of the unknown’ phenomena afforded to low-fidelity titles like 1999's Silent Hill . (There’s an entire genre of indie horror games that pursue this aesthetic for a reason, after all.)

Speaking with Gamespot , producer Hidemaro Fujibayashi explained that the Remake’s updated graphics actually made the ReDeads extremely scary at first. And while the development team was supposedly enthusiastic about this aspect of the project, he and fellow producer Eiji Aonuma felt that this detail wasn’t necessarily true to the original experience of the first game.

"With this remake, the graphics are a lot improved, and so the ReDead – the sound, the graphics, and the movement – ended up being very, very scary,” Fujibayashi said. “And the staff wanted to make this in service of making a good gameplay experience. But from our perspective, taking a step back, we felt like, ‘Let's remember the experience that we don't want to change, and taking that into consideration, maybe we've gone a step too far, so let's dial it back.’"

That being said, plenty of players feel that the Remake’s ReDeads are still sufficiently terrifying. Social media is rife with hilarious reactions from fans’ first encounters with the enemies, with both Western and Japanese players having a “nope, f**k this,” mentality after first coming across them in the game.

news.title: Fredrik Wester 第二次辞职后，Paradox Interactive 迎来了新老板
news.summary: Deputy CEO Mattias Lilja is taking the reins in January.

content.v: Paradox Interactive is getting a new boss: Deputy CEO Mattias Lilja will take over from current CEO Fredrik Wester in January 2027, a move Paradox said "is a natural evolution of how the company is already led."
"My plan was never to be CEO for life. The goal was to build the foundation before passing the baton on for the next chapter in the company’s journey," Wester said in today's announcement .

"Since I returned as CEO, we’ve streamlined our strategy, rebuilt our pipeline and developed our commercial offering. Mattias has had a central role in laying this foundation, and now is the right time to hand over. Given his experience and vision, he is exceptionally well positioned to take the company to its next level."

As his statement implies, this is his second tenure as Paradox CEO: He held the position from 2009 to 2018, when he resigned and was replaced by Ebba Ljungerud. But Ljungerud's tenure was rocky, and she resigned in 2021 over "differing views on the company's strategy going forward," at which point Wester returned to the role.

In many ways, Lilja has been calling the CEO shots for a few years now anyway, while Wester's focus has increasingly been on Paradox's "long-term development and goals." And he, like Wester, is also a returnee: He left the company in 2020 after five years in various executive roles, but returned in 2021 along with Wester as "chief of staff." Lilja's LinkedIn profile says his primary duty was to "support the Paradox CEO in leading the executive team, aligning the strategic plan with the day to day operations," and that he would "act as the stand-in for the CEO when needed."

"I approach this role with great humility," Lilja said. "Paradox has a unique DNA that has made us one of the greats in deep and engaging strategy and management games. Now we’re stepping up the pace: we will make further investments in our core business, push the boundaries of our game design, work even more closely with our loyal players, develop more and better tools and services that benefit both modders and players, and continue to sharpen our ways of working and our organisation, with player value in focus."

Reaction among the Paradox community on Reddit seems guarded at this point, which is perhaps understandable given how it went the time the company got a new CEO. PC Gamer's Fraser Brown took a deep dive into that in his 2024 report on " the Dark Age of Paradox Interactive ," which includes thoughts from Lilja on the "challenges" of success and what he saw as the future of Paradox.

Even back then, Lilja was clearly helping chart the company's course, and there's also some optimism among Paradox follower in the fact that he seems likely to carry on in Wester's footsteps—and an apparent understanding that Wester has been eyeing the door for a while now anyway.

news.title: 两款同名游戏的美好结局令任天堂头疼
news.summary: On November 25, two entirely separate games called Piece by Piece are releasing on Nintendo Switch. It's no co

content.v: On November 25, two entirely separate games called Piece by Piece are releasing on Nintendo Switch. It's no coincidence, but the circumstances that led to this unusual situation certainly stem from a coincidence.

Publisher No More Robots launched Piece by Piece, a cozy sim game full of cute animal characters, on Steam back in March. Two days later, studio Neon Polygons self-published an unrelated puzzle-platformer where you jump through literal puzzle pieces that you connect together--this game is also called Piece by Piece.

What could have been a conflict between indie developers turned out to be the beginning of a wholesome business relationship. Both games were bundled together on Steam , and now No More Robots is publishing the Switch ports of both titles.

According to No More Robots co-founder Mike Rose, Neon Polygons "couldn't afford to bring their game to Switch," so No More Robots stepped in to publish the game for them. As with Steam, you can buy both games together in a bundle .

It's undeniably a heartwarming and unique story, though one would assume that having to figure out the logistics behind launching two games that not only have the same name, but the same release date and publisher as well, was a nightmare on the backend of the Nintendo eShop.

"And yes, Nintendo have ABSOLUTELY HATED THIS," Rose said in a social media post, adding that the publisher was questioned why it had two games with the same name "many, many times." At least the bundle doesn't also include the Pharrell Williams Lego movie Piece by Piece as well.

news.title: 韩国游戏评级委员会差点阻止《GTA 6》的发行，担心其“断章取义的生殖器裸露”会“扰乱社会秩序”
news.summary: GTA 6 required a total of three ratings reviews by South Korea's GCRB—and Cyberleek might have had something t

others.title: 《GTA 6》因“生殖器裸露”差点在韩国被拒绝评级

content.v: Grand Theft Auto 6 has been granted an Adults Only rating in South Korea by the country's Game Content Rating Board . But in the weeks preceding that decision, the board had nearly refused to issue the game an age rating—effectively leaving it ineligible for sale in South Korea—due to ratings officials' concerns that GTA 6 might be way too comfortable hanging unprompted hog.

According to GCRB meeting minutes obtained by South Korean outlet Inven (via Kotaku ), GTA 6 required a total of three ratings reviews, in which committee members repeatedly debated the presence of what they described as "out-of-context genital nudity"—a perception that seemed to have been informed by the leaked GTA 6 developer build footage circulated by cryptopeddling cornball master criminal, Cyberleek .
https://cdn.mos.cms.futurecdn.net/MSGVughAzWDrkRvPx5QzJF-1920-80.jpg

The GCRB's initial rating review for GTA 6 took place on September 10, during which committee members argued over whether the game's "out-of-context genital nudity" was grounds for refusal. Previously, the GCRB's rating standards automatically rejected games with exposed genitalia, but those standards were relaxed in 2025 to permit an Adults Only rating for "cases where suggestive bodily exposure is directly and specifically depicted," as long as that depiction didn't extend to graphic sexual acts.

Despite that revision, the committee members arguing to refuse an age rating for GTA 6 said that, while the GCRB had previously permitted "a certain degree of genital exposure where there is narrative justification," they "did not believe genital exposure to this extent falls within acceptable limits."

As the report notes, that first review meeting occurred before the GCRB received a playable GTA 6 build, meaning that the GCRB members' perception of the extent of visible in-game genitalia could have been informed by Cyberleek's leaked footage of an in-game nudist colony —an area that, despite the abundance of human flesh on display, didn't actually entail much sex going on. It was mostly just nude people standing around doing people things.
https://cdn.mos.cms.futurecdn.net/eJo5P8BDBGovE2QsQ5Xy3F-1920-80.jpg

The GCRB committee members in favor of an Adults Only rating noted as much, saying that "in this game, scenes with heavy exposure are not particularly sexual," while "conversely, in sexual scenes, exposure is limited." The first meeting ended in a 3-3 tie vote, leading the committee to postpone its decision and instead recommend to Rockstar that the game be modified.

The GCRB did eventually receive a playable build of GTA 6 on September 28—just six days before its scheduled second review meeting on October 2. While an initial report from its gameplay researcher indicated that "genital exposure scenes mostly appeared as one-off mission backgrounds and did not lead to sexual interactions," the committee decided to once again postpone its decision simply because the game was too damn huge for it to be confident that it had seen all the relevant cases of penises and/or vulvas in the wild.

A few on the committee remained skeptical, however: "The basic principle of rating refusal applies when bodily exposure of sexual acts are depicted explicitly or excessively so as to disrupt social order," one GCRB committee member said. "By that standard, the current bodily exposure is sufficiently explicit and excessive."
https://cdn.mos.cms.futurecdn.net/3sHZC8NBR3b3njThA3iVHF-1920-80.jpg

In its third and final review meeting on October 16, the GCRB—informed in part by the fact that 10 other institutions like the US's ESRB and Europe's PEGI had issued their own ratings—ultimately voted 8-1 in favor of granting GTA 6 an Adults Only rating. Its researchers concluded that, after playing the game more thoroughly, scenes featuring full-frontal nudity didn't allow for any sexual interaction, and that cutscene sequences where protagonists Jason and Lucia did do sex at each other didn't expose any genitalia.

Interestingly, the GCRB researchers also confirmed that they couldn't replicate the ability to fully strip Jason and Lucia of their clothes that was shown in Cyberleek videos, inadvertently confirming that the GTA 6 build that'll be available to the public won't allow players to roam Vice City in the nude. Apologies if you were particularly invested in seeing Jason's dong.

And additional apologies to the one dissenting GCRB member who still voted for refusing an age rating for GTA 6, in part due to their fear that the rating could serve as precedent for other genres, meaning "background genital exposure will frequently appear in future RPGs as a result." I suspect they're going to have a rough time once Divinity comes out .

news.title: Xbox 花了 25 年时间追踪你的游戏习惯；现在您可以看到损坏情况
news.summary: It's the 25th anniversary of Xbox, and to celebrate, you can see how much time you've spent--or wasted, accord

content.v: It's the 25th anniversary of Xbox, and to celebrate, you can see how much time you've spent--or wasted, according to my parents--playing games on Xbox hardware over the years. Not to be confused with the end-of-year wrap-up that Xbox usually offers, Xbox Playback looks at your entire history, from when you first booted up a console to your current-day Achievements.

It's a neat little celebratory feature, complete with a customized video and graphics that you can show off. In addition to the date you started playing on Xbox, it includes the first Xbox console you used, the first game you booted up, your total hours played, a breakdown of game genres, and more. (There are some limits on data during Xbox's early years, though.) You can try it out by signing in to your Xbox account through this link .
https://www.gamespot.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/11/Xbox-stats.jpg?w=636

Other stats you can check out include the games you spent the most hours on, which ones you got a 100% Achievement rank in, and your longest streak of consecutive play days. Xbox says you can share your record online by scanning a QR code at the end of the video that plays--just in case you want to share how many hours you've sunk into Viva Piñata over the decades.

While this is a fun way to look back at your Xbox history, it does come at a bittersweet time for Microsoft's gaming brand. This year has been brutal for Xbox employees amid a grand "reset" spearheaded by Xbox CEO Asha Sharma, as scores of jobs have been lost and several game studios have left the company. Xbox is now focused on chasing big hits across PC, consoles, and mobile, with an ambitious goal of becoming more profitable than its biggest gaming rivals, Sony and Nintendo, by 2030.

Sharma has also written about what the next 25 years for Xbox could look like, with her open letter suggesting that artificial intelligence will play a greater role in the future of video game development.

news.title: 《最终幻想 14》玩家哀悼游戏传奇贝斯手的离去
news.summary: The Final Fantasy 14 community is in mourning following news that Eikichi Iwai, the bassist for the game's hou

content.v: The Final Fantasy 14 community is in mourning following news that Eikichi Iwai, the bassist for the game's house band, The Primals, has died at the age of 57, and is taking to the MMORPG's main hub cities to honor his legacy.

An "Important Announcement" post on the official FF14 website from developer Square Enix on November 11 broke the news, and stated the development team was "deeply saddened" to inform the community of Iwai's passing.

"Having witnessed his truly unforgettable performance on stage at the recent Final Fantasy 14 Fan Festival in Japan, the sudden news of his passing has come as a profound shock," the statement reads. "The members of The Primals and the entire FF14 development and operations team are overcome with deep sorrow.
"As we reflect on all that Eikichi-san has left behind, our thoughts are with him, and we offer our heartfelt condolences."
https://www.gamespot.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/11/The-Primals.jpg?w=636

The Primals, composed of Iwai on bass, composer Masayoshi Soken, localization lead Michael-Christopher Koji Fox, and band members Tetsuya Tachibana and GUNN, are behind some of FF14's most memorable tracks. Iwai's bass in particular stands out on songs like Shadowbringers' To the Edge and Stormblood's Amatsu Kaze . The band performed worldwide at various FF14 Fan Festivals, as well as at a UK rock festival , earlier this year.

Final Fantasy 14's community has a reputation as being one of the best, and most welcoming, in gaming, so it's no surprise it took the time to honor Iwai's passing. As spotted on Reddit , the game's playerbase has come together to pay their respects Iwai, with large gatherings of players holding firelight vigils in his memory across the game's various servers and cities.
"It's so good to see everyone come together, he deserves it for playing such a big role in the music we've fallen in love with. May he rest peacefully," one community member wrote .
More of Iwai and The Primals' music will be heard in Final Fantasy 14's next upcoming expansion, Evercold, set to release on February 23, 2027.

news.title: Xbox 首席执行官在微软游戏机 25 周年之际展望未来：“一个人很快就能掌握曾经需要整个国家才能完成的能力”
news.summary: Asha Sharma doesn't specifically mention AI in her 25th anniversary message, but I'm pretty sure that's what s

content.v: In a message marking the 25th anniversary of the first Xbox console , Xbox CEO Asha Sharma predicts that the future of gaming will look much like its beginning, "when a small team with a big idea could change how the world plays." And even though the term never actually appears in her post, yeah, I'm pretty sure she's talking about AI.

Sharma's message kicks off with a blast from the early days of Microsoft, beginning with a look at Microsoft Adventure, an adaptation of Colossal Cave "that looked more like MS-DOS than an early version of Minecraft," and the first-ever Microsoft staff photo that showcases some absolutely spectacular hair. From there it's a quick trip through Microsoft Flight Simulator, Quake, DirectX, and then in 2001, the original Xbox.

Naturally, there's a tribute to the "generations of employees, studios, developers, and partners" who helped create and grow Xbox, and the people who have played on various generations of consoles over the years.

"Since joining Xbox, I've heard stories of friendships that began over a session and lasted a lifetime, of people who met the person they would marry, and of parents now sharing the games they grew up on with their children," Sharma writes. "I've also heard about people who are no longer with us, and how much those hours spent playing together still mean to those who love them. Ultimately, this is why we exist."

From there, Sharma offers thoughts on the future of Xbox, and this is where I think it gets interesting: After comparing the size and capabilities of the original Microsoft Flight Simulator with the 2024 edition, she continues, "While modern games demonstrate the heights of human craft in ways unimaginable just decades ago, the cost, resources, and risk required to create them have grown just as dramatically. As a result, too many ideas never become games, and too many games fall short of what their creators imagined. For decades, this has been the unavoidable tradeoff of ambition. We must change this."
How exactly that change will come about goes unspecified, but my guess? She's talking about AI.
"Throughout human history, the scale of what we could create was determined by the people, capital, and resources we could command. That relationship is beginning to break," Sharma writes.

"A single person will soon be able to wield capabilities that once required entire nations. A small team will be able to build worlds that today demand hundreds of developers and hundreds of millions of dollars. And our largest studios will be able to pursue ambitions as far beyond today’s games as Microsoft Flight Simulator 2024 is from its first entry in 1982."

The explosive rise in the cost of game development is undeniable. The pioneering open-world sci-fi RPG Starflight was literally made by five guys; its distant descendant Mass Effect: Andromeda credits 14 people for working on "audio design" alone. Take-Two CEO Strauss Zelnick summed up the situation quite aptly earlier this year, calling big-budget game development "a high-stakes game for big boys only "; the development budget of the upcoming Grand Theft Auto 6 is being talked about in terms of billions.

Despite Sharma's optimistic presentation, though, I'm not entirely confident that an AI-powered future where one person—or even a few—can do what currently takes hundreds is really a desirable outcome.

Alongside questions of ethics and artistic vision, there are also very pragmatic concerns about the long-term future of the games industry itself. Because really, the embrace of AI—not just at Xbox, but everywhere—is about cutting jobs. Bethesda had nine concept artists working on Starfield: What happens when somebody in an office decides they can get the same job done, pretty much , with two guys hammering out prompts? Maybe even just one? Quarterly profits and shareholder return may go up, but I doubt we'll be saying the same about the quality of the games we play.

Sharma concluded by writing that she believes "the future of gaming will look more like its beginning, when a small team with a big idea could change how the world plays." I would argue that small teams are already doing that—the big, billion-dollar blockbusters that have prompted these worries seem far more committed to merely giving us more of what we've already got.

content.v: I'm modding GTA 5 every day in a quest to either transform it into a PC version of GTA 6 or break it entirely. Come back tomorrow to find out what new horrible thing I've done to Rockstar's baby, or check out what I got up to earlier .

The police, GTA 5 informs me, have my description. This is not a surprise; everyone has my description. I have installed Everyone Is Franklin , and now everyone is Franklin. Or, well, nearly everyone is Franklin. Here is a comprehensive list of entities who are not Franklin:

Everyone else? Franklin. All of Los Santos has become me, morphing into my tasteful cashmere jumper and chinos. They lounge on street corners, louche and smoking. They occupy the beachfront gym, sweating through that same cashmere as they bench press and kickbox. They are everywhere. I am everywhere. I can give myself a piggyback if I want to. I do want to.
https://cdn.mos.cms.futurecdn.net/4LXh9HVa59CUWTpatzjei8-1920-80.gif

It's actually a bit disconcerting. The streets are somewhat emptier now, for reasons unknown to me, and those Franklins who remain to populate it are mostly very quiet. They shuffle along in mute procession. To where? I know not. Some new world, maybe, glimpsed in a dream.

One wrinkle is that, in becoming Franklin, it seems every single person in Los Santos has also inherited Franklin's divine un-life. They are all unkillable. No matter how many explosives I lay at their feet or how many cars flatten them, they get up and keep on trucking. Also, I cannot aim directly at any of them. They are my allies. Am I my own ally? A philosophical question. Sometimes, surely, I am my own worst enemy.

news.summary: When Halo: Campaign Evolved first came out in July it did not include any multiplayer modes, but the first-per

content.v: https://assets-prd.ignimgs.com/2026/11/12/halo-1794505816407.jpg
When Halo: Campaign Evolved first came out in July it did not include any multiplayer modes, but the first-person shooter remake will at least get Firefight as a free update this winter.
Xbox CEO Asha Sharma announced the returning mode in a social media post Thursday, along with a graphic showing a team of Spartans shooting a mix of Covenant and Flood enemies with various guns.

While Firefight isn't the arena competitive multiplayer that most fans had hoped from the Halo remake at launch, wave-based PvE has been a mainstay in the series since Halo 3: ODST in 2009. Essentially, you and your friends load into a map and fight increasingly difficult waves of enemies until you get overwhelmed. There's no reason to believe that this iteration is going to be any different.

Regardless of whether or not Team Deathmatch comes to Halo: Campaign Evolved, this will be the first multiplayer mode to hit the remake, which was pitched primarily as a straight-up revival of the iconic Combat Evolved campaign. Multiplayer was the major piece missing from Campaign Evolved, and this could be a sign that more multiplayer modes will be added in the future.

IGN's Halo: Combat Evolved remake gave it a 7 . We said: "Halo: Campaign Evolved speaks to the series' timelessness and adds a decent set of new missions, but it's a mostly a lean retread that's more of a test run for its future with Unreal Engine."

This Firefight announcement comes as Xbox celebrates its 25th anniversary. Earlier today, Sharma looked ahead, predicting "a single person will soon be able to wield capabilities that once required entire nations."

As for Halo, following the summer's drastic cuts at Microsoft's gaming business, Xbox announced a significant reshuffle that saw the next mainline Halo game handed to Call of Duty developer Activision , which is spinning up a new team to work on the franchise. Mass layoffs hit Halo Studios at the same time.

news.summary: Huang's permanent replacement will have some massive shoes to fill.

content.v: Has there ever been a tech CEO quite like Jensen Huang? The Nvidia chief has been an emblematic figure to PC gamers for years, before transcending into one of the primary architects of the AI revolution. Regardless of whether you love or hate the technology, (and the financial behemoth that Nvidia has become), you have to admit that Huang has presided over a meteoric rise to the top, the likes of which the tech world has rarely seen.

Now Huang, the Nvidia cofounder, figurehead, and global AI industry pillar, has announced his resignation . The admission of an affair with someone some people suspect to be a Chinese spy, followed days later by reports of another affair with an Nvidia employee, proved to be his undoing as Nvidia chief.

Nvidia's share price has dropped significantly in recent weeks. Investors, likely looking for some sort of stability after the past few weeks of AI and tech company financial woes, seem shaken. In many ways, the situation is unprecedented, and it's hard to draw parallels. But now Huang has gone, it puts Nvidia in the unenviable position of finding someone to replace him at the top of the stack.

Nvidia CFO Colette Kress has taken over as interim CEO for now, but the board will almost certainly be trying to avoid a situation where it ends up with a revolving door of bosses over the next few years.

Which brings me on to Intel, which has found itself working through CEOs at a surprising rate over the past couple of decades. While there are obvious downsides to having a single, totemic figure at the top of a company structure, flat or otherwise, swapping them out on a regular basis isn't necessarily good for business, either.
https://cdn.mos.cms.futurecdn.net/nMeckmewJ3aD8PjFumN8Um-1920-80.jpg

Intel enjoyed a good run of stability under CEO Paul Otellini, who served as Intel chief from 2005 to 2013. He was then succeeded by Brian Krzanich. He became Intel's CEO in 2013, after joining the company in 1982 and working his way to the top. His tenure was not regarded as a particularly successful one due to stagnation in development, but the Intel ship continued to sail onwards for the next five years regardless.

Then Intel learned that Krzanich had been engaged in a consensual relationship with an employee , an interesting echo of current events. After the board decided this was in violation of Intel's non-fraternisation policy, Krzanich resigned. And so Intel's quest to find a suitable CEO began again. As a temporary solution, previous chief financial officer Bob Swan took over the top seat in 2019, although reportedly reluctantly .

Swan's time as Intel chief was marred by manufacturing setbacks , which allowed TSMC and AMD to pull ahead in terms of market share. Financially, though, Intel continued with strong performance—perhaps expected with a finance guy at the helm. Still, a more permanent CEO needed to be found.
https://cdn.mos.cms.futurecdn.net/hFHTnKCwmtBsH4LDrAug7Y-1920-80.jpg

The company eventually landed on Pat Gelsinger. Gelsinger began his career at Intel at just 18-years-old, before working his way up to the CTO position over a 30-year-period. After a stint at EMC as president and chief operating officer (and later CEO of VMware), Gelsinger took over the reins of Intel in 2021.

Gelsinger's strategy for the company (in the face of fierce market competition) was based on a stunningly ambitious roadmap of five process nodes in five years , while focussing on Intel's foundry business. He famously once said that he'd " bet the whole company " on its then-upcoming 18A process node.

However, more manufacturing delays, workforce cuts, and a broken consumer CPU scandal were just some of the issues faced by the company towards the end of Gelsinger's reign. This super ambitious roadmap, in combination with these factors and others, led to poor financial results for Intel , and Gelsinger retired at the end of 2024 .
https://cdn.mos.cms.futurecdn.net/gywvJokCYFrGaCdJJFwopR-1920-80.png

This then led to CFO David Zinsner and Intel executive Michelle Johnson Holthaus leading the company in co-CEO roles until 2025, when current CEO Lip-Bu Tan was brought in . Tan set about reorganizing the company, changing its structure so that engineering departments reported directly to him. "They [had] too many silos, too many people needed reporting. And even though they come to the CEO, they are not paying attention to it," said Tan in May of this year about the previous company structure.

"So I decided the best thing is to really understand where the problem is," Tan continued, "so that I can focus on the engineering, how to redesign, [how to] simplify the products, and then get the real killer product out."

Intel has reported extremely strong financial results under Tan's leadership , after a deal signed with the US government to steady the financial ship—although the company took a significant knock in the recent tech share sell off due to its position in the data center CPU market. However, while Tan now looks to be firmly in place at Intel, the company's ride through the market over the past two decades has undoubtedly been a bumpy one.
And still pretty bumpy today. It recently cut its sales outlook as the PC market flounders thanks to AI eating up all the RAM, and its share price plummeted as a result.
https://cdn.mos.cms.futurecdn.net/6xW3ucQoEZYyTScKwHvWDF-1920-80.jpg

Finding a CEO with Jensen Huang's level of influence, public profile, and ability to lead the company to ever-greater heights seems near impossible. Whoever leads Nvidia next will step into truly gigantic shoes, and in the face of an AI market that looks increasingly wobbly, they'll need to be the right person for the job. And swapping leaders out on the regular? Well, it's taken its toll on Intel over the years, that's for sure.

All of which must weigh heavily upon those sitting underneath the big green logo in Santa Clara, working out exactly who the next CEO should be. Not the least bit with the US government already making its thoughts clear on who might take the job. It's not easy, running a massive tech corporation, that much is clear. And in the modern world, they don't come much bigger than Nvidia.

news.title: Darktide 将于 12 月 7 日举办“战斗姐妹”课程
news.summary: Technically a Sister Novitiate but still.

content.v: Warhammer 40,000: Darktide has announced its newest class, the Sister Novitiate , is arriving on December 7, finally bringing the much anticipated Adepta Sororitas faction to Atoma. Alongside the Skitarii, which was the last class added, the Sisters of Battle have been long–requested by players.

Also similar to the Skitarii, this class has a slightly different design to the other rejects. The Sisters Novitiate can choose from six Acts of Faith instead of blitz and combat abilities, drawing on a new "Faith" resource to use an offensive Neural Whip, or more support based abilities like the Icon of Purity and protective prayers.

Essentially, sisters build their faith through combat via Doctrines and Pledges within the talent tree, which change how it's accrued, allowing them to then unleash up to two chosen Acts of Faith. It sounds fairly similar to the Skitarii's somewhat looser skill and ability tree.
In terms of weapons, we can look forward to:

There's also a meltagun (the first in Darktide), which will be added as a free update alongside for the Veteran class to also use. I'm personally pretty excited for the Condemnor Stake Thrower, a crossbow which pins enemies in place, and as a Zealot main, a new chainsword in the form of the Penitent Eviscerator. There'll likely be a fair bit of crossover between the Zealot and Sister Novitiate.

Overall, this new class is a clever way of including the Adepta Sororitas in Darktide. Lore wise, it would make little sense for a full Sister of Battle to be running around with convicts and rejects, but a sister-in-training, sure, why not?
You can find the new class on Steam where it's set to cost €12 (so I assume £10/$12, the same as the Skitarii was) when it launches on December 7.

news.title: 黄仁勋从英伟达辞职后，人们对这位前首席执行官的评价要么是赞扬，要么是政治上的相互指责，几乎没有中间的内容。
news.summary: Sadness is the general sentiment, it seems.

content.v: Welp, that's it, the face of Nvidia is no longer the face of Nvidia. Jensen Huang served as CEO of the company since it was founded over three decades ago, and now he's out, replaced by the new interim CEO Colette Kress, who was previously Chief Financial Officer ( exactly what we predicted , by the way).

This is in the wake of two affair scandals surrounding the former CEO. The first affair Huang admitted to , and it's alleged that the other party in the tango is a lady who is currently accused of being a Chinese spy. The second is a reported affair that Huang allegedly had with Nvidia's VP of healthcare , Kimberly Powell.

Many people expected Huang's resignation in the lead-up to this, so it is no big surprise that it has now been announced by Nvidia . But now that it's official, the response has largely been as expected: a combination of disappointment at his resignation and praise for his time as Nvidia CEO.

President Trump certainly expressed as much , saying Huang has done a "fantastic job." Trump also has a suggestion for who should take over: ex-Apple CEO Tim Cook: "Now that Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang, who has done a fantastic job, has resigned, there is only one man to take his place - Tim Cook of Apple. A Legend replaces a Legend! President Donald J. Trump."
https://cdn.mos.cms.futurecdn.net/VudtZ5MuP4XCQEotX3eGg9-1920-80.jpg
Hugging Face co-founder Clement Delangue expresses the general sentiment : "This whole thing sucks, and I wish none of it had happened. It’s a really sad day!"

This whole thing sucks, and I wish none of it had happened. It’s a really sad day!But I want to make one thing clear: we’ll keep fighting for open-source AI, harder than ever. This is too important to slow down now. Let’s go! November 12, 2026

Nvidia recently set out to buy Hugging Face , the open-source AI platform, and given the latter agreed, it makes sense for the company to assuage any fears over the news of Huang's resignation. Julien Chaumond, Hugging Face co-founder and CTO, has expressed that "the mission has not and will not change."

Epic Games CEO Tim Sweeney has expressed his sadness , too: "A sad day for Nvidia, developers, America, and all humanity. Jensen founded and ran one of the few companies to reach a massive scale while driving massive continued innovation and ubiquity, while others fell into the trap of ever-increasing extraction."

A sad day for NVIDIA, developers, America, and all humanity. Jensen founded and ran one of the few companies to reach a massive scale while driving massive continued innovation and ubiquity, while others fell into the trap of ever-increasing extraction. November 12, 2026

Sweeney's response isn't a surprise. Before Huang's resignation was announced, both Tim Sweeney and Elon Musk certainly expressed high praise for Huang. The former said, "This would be an Apple firing Steve Jobs level of idiocy from Nvidia’s board if they did that, and a grievous harm to the United States of America." And the latter said it would be "an honor" to hire him.

It's also no surprise, then, that the Epic CEO has banged the same drum a few additional times since the announcement, calling it "far too much government heavy handedness" and taking a dig at Nvidia's new interim CEO for waiting a week until discussing everything in a company meeting.
Even ancient file-sharing platform LimeWire has jumped in on the news .
jensen huang come work at limewire we don't care who you date just bring the leather jacket November 12, 2026

Over the past couple of days before the resignation, there were differing opinions on whether Huang should resign or not. Some thought so, but the more general sentiment across social media seemed to be that regardless of any alleged affairs, he is a good CEO and it will be very damaging for Nvidia to lose him.
The reactions now, in the wake of Huang's resignation, seem to concur.
That is, apart from the US Select Committee on China, which is decidedly more stern :

"Jensen Huang’s firing from the company he founded is an unfortunate end that could have been avoided. It is in our national interest for NVIDIA and our other AI champions to succeed, but American companies should never jeopardize our nation’s security by giving Chinese companies access to their most advanced chips. Nvidia must now change its corporate practices and appoint leadership that makes national security its top priority. In Congress we must act quickly to pass bipartisan export control legislation in the year-end national defense bill."
Chairman @RepMoolenaar released the following statement in the wake of Jensen Huang's resignation from @NVIDIA: https://t.co/sCJIYnE7Wo November 12, 2026

The political bigwigs in general will be looking to get from this whatever they can. New York senator and Senate Democratic Leader Chuck Schumer says , "Despite Jensen Huang’s resignation, Congress must demand answers from Mr. Huang and others at Nvidia about how they may have put U.S. national security at risk."

Despite Jensen Huang’s resignation, Congress must demand answers from Mr. Huang and others at Nvidia about how they may have put U.S. national security at risk. The Trump administration must also answer for what it did once it learned about Mr. Huang’s relationship with a suspected Chinese intelligence asset. Were government officials told not to investigate because of Trump’s relationship with Mr. Huang? What did Trump know when he personally invited Mr. Huang aboard Air Force One? Americans deserve to know that those at the highest levels of power are putting America first, not their bottom line or their personal friendships. November 12, 2026

As far as we're concerned as PC gamers, much of this might be by-the-by. Whoever heads up Nvidia, the company long since stopped putting gaming anywhere near the centre of its focus. AI is the name of the game, now.

I can't help but feel a little sad, though. Huang has been one of the biggest names in PC gaming hardware for decades, but no longer. Whatever you think of the man himself and whether he should have resigned, there is indeed something sad about his era being over.

news.title: 前首席执行官黄仁勋被罢黜后，英伟达股价回升
news.summary: Nvidia's share price has seemingly grown by around 10% since pre-market trading lows.

content.v: This week has been a mess for Nvidia, with its CEO, Jensen Huang, admitting to an affair on Sunday , only for a second affair allegation to come out yesterday . Today, Nvidia shares started as low as $151 in pre-market trading, but have since bounced back to between $163 and $166 in the opening hours of Nasdaq trading after the announcement of Jensen Huang's retirement as CEO .

One might assume a downward trajectory with Huang's resignation, and CFO Colette Kress replacing him, as it could flag instability to shareholders, but the stock price now sits where it once sat on Wednesday, November 11 at 5 PM ET. The Nvidia stock price has been unruly this week, dipping by $15 between Friday night and Monday morning, then climbing to $181 by the end of Monday, then once again dropping to $167 on Tuesday.

But, importantly, this morning saw the worst trade open for Nvidia stock since June 2025, just before the memory crisis started. The jump from $151 to around $165 represents a 10% increase for the company.

Naturally, stocks are a fickle business, and, famously, the 'dead cat bounce' effect describes a moment in a stock decline where it briefly recovers. But Nvidia, even with a big loss in market cap value, is still an incredibly successful company worth multiple trillions of dollars at the time of writing.

I had my eye on the trading value this morning, somewhat expecting a decline after the opening, given the drop overnight, and it's easy to see why. Jensen Huang is a cofounder of Nvidia, which at one point was the most valuable company in the world. He has been the president and CEO of the company since 1993, and he's no doubt been instrumental in the business and its success.

This whole thing sucks, and I wish none of it had happened. It’s a really sad day!But I want to make one thing clear: we’ll keep fighting for open-source AI, harder than ever. This is too important to slow down now. Let’s go! November 12, 2026

And this morning, many big names in the tech industry expressed their sadness at his departure. Tim Sweeney, the Epic Games founder and CEO, said it was "A sad day for Nvidia, developers, America, and all humanity", and Clement Delangue, the co-founder and CEO of AI platform Hugging Face, said , "This whole thing sucks, and I wish none of it had happened. It’s a really sad day". Jim Cramer, the host of Mad Money on CNBC, said "Jensen we hardly knew yah. Just plain awful...."

Colette Kress has taken over , but only in the interim, and Nvidia is no doubt shopping around for the person who will replace Huang. Bets are open on who exactly that person could be, from the CEO of Intel, AMD, and Arm, all the way to Elon Musk . And Donald Trump even wants ex-Apple CEO Tim Cook to take the chair . It's anyone's guess, really, and a good sign that it's also hard to guess exactly what will happen when it comes to stock prices.

news.title: 新的 GTA 6 游戏内镜头继续凸显游戏令人难以置信的图像
news.summary: Rockstar has released yet another in-game clip from GTA 6, and like yesterday's footage, fans can't quite beli

content.v: https://assets-prd.ignimgs.com/2026/11/12/ultimate-edition-grotti-cheetah-02-1794504940864.jpg
Rockstar has released yet another in-game clip from GTA 6 , and like yesterday's footage, fans can't quite believe it's real.

This morning, the Instagram account "Only in Dade" (which posts real videos from around Miami, Florida) shared a video of several flashy cars driving around. However, this footage isn't real life; it's actually GTA 6 footage.

The page posted footage of these cars sitting on GTA 6's version of Ocean Drive yesterday while a group of NPCs observed them. Yesterday's footage was actually an in-game recreation of a real video that was posted in October, showing Rockstar's real-life marketing efforts in Miami. Presumably, the new video posted today is also a recreation of a real video from when the real versions of these cars were zooming around the city.

Although the footage doesn't show much, it is an extremely impressive showcase of GTA 6's graphical fidelity. When the first clip dropped yesterday, many thought it was AI or some kind of render. However, it has since been confirmed as authentic gameplay and was reposted by Rockstar itself on Instagram. Fans have reacted to both clips in awe of the visuals, noting that the game has really outdone itself.

"Absolutely insane this is in-game," said one fan in response to the new footage. "This game isn't real, bro; there HAS to be a trap somewhere. There is no f**king way," said another fan in disbelief .

Some have even joked that if this is really how the final game looks, they're more than happy to play it at 30fps . It's clear that Rockstar traded higher performance in favor of visual fidelity, and while that may not be what some fans want, it is inevitably going to result in one of the most graphically advanced games we have ever seen.

Today officially marks exactly one week until GTA 6's release. The game is available to preload right now and it is tracking to have one of the biggest launches in entertainment history. Xbox and PlayStation both confirmed that the game is the most preordered title in the history of their respective stores , and analysts have estimated that the game has already surpassed $1 billion in sales ahead of launch.

Speaking of launch, some game developers are giving their staff the week off to play the game. Palworld developer Pocketpair is one such studio happy to provide extra holiday for the occasion . IGN's latest coverage includes speculation about a potential beloved legacy character from a previous game hiding in the latest GTA 6 trailer .

news.title: Xbox 首席执行官的 25 周年纪念信息是关于人工智能的，即使她不会说出来
news.summary: As Xbox celebrates its 25th anniversary, Xbox CEO Asha Sharma has shared her thoughts on where gaming is going

content.v: As Xbox celebrates its 25th anniversary, Xbox CEO Asha Sharma has shared her thoughts on where gaming is going over the next 25 years, and people are saying her message is really more about pushing AI.

Sharma said modern games demonstrate the "heights of human craft in ways unimaginable just decades ago." However, the costs, resources, and risks that companies need to take on have "grown just as dramatically," she said.

"As a result, too many ideas never become games, and too many games fall short of what their creators imagined. For decades, this has been the unavoidable tradeoff of ambition. We must change this," she said.
https://www.gamespot.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/11/Xbox25.jpg?w=636

Historically, to create anything at scale required immense resources, but Sharma said that's changing. Without saying AI, Sharma said it won't be long until a single person can "wield capabilities that once required entire nations."

"A small team will be able to build worlds that today demand hundreds of developers and hundreds of millions of dollars. And our largest studios will be able to pursue ambitions as far beyond today’s games as Microsoft Flight Simulator 2024 is from its first entry in 1982," she said.

Sharma went on to say that the future of gaming "will look more like its beginning," which is to say that a small team with a bold idea can make a real impact. "Our responsibility is to deliver great games, unmistakable hardware, and give more people the chance to make something the world has never seen," she said.

Xbox recently launched Xbox Labs, which is a pretty obvious push into the world of vibe-coded games . Sharma has promised that she has "no tolerance for bad AI." She added, “We will not chase short-term efficiency or flood our ecosystem with soulless AI slop.”

Sharma became Xbox CEO earlier this year, replacing Phil Spencer. Sharma immediately made lots of big changes to "reset" the business, including mass layoffs, game cancellations, and studio closures/divestitures.

Sharma comes from an AI background, having previously been an executive on the CoreAI team at Microsoft. She may be bullish about having smaller teams make big games going forward, but it's not an all-or-nothing approach. After all, Xbox continues to own and fund large-scale, expensive productions like Call of Duty, World of Warcraft, and Forza just to name a few.

AI is a big push for Xbox's owner, Microsoft, so it makes sense to see Sharma undertake efforts to increase Xbox's own efforts in that department. This is happening after a study of game developers found that more developers than ever think generative AI is bad for gaming.

content.v: It's the end of an era for Nvidia , as its founder and longtime CEO, Jensen Huang, has resigned effective immediately. The face of one of the largest companies in the US and the growing AI boom, Huang's retirement comes after news broke of his two extramarital affairs, one of which was with a suspected Chinese spy.

Nvidia has appointed its Chief Financial Officer, Colette Kress, to serve as interim CEO and Harvey C. Jones as Chair of the Board, but Huang's departure will leave a void that won't be easily filled, as he was heavily involved in Nvidia's day-to-day operations.

The news is also expected to complicate things for Nvidia's stock price, as it has been in decline for over a month. The internet is already having a field day with Huang's departure, with hot takes and memes dominating the discourse right now. Huang's days of pulling on his signature leather jacket and hitting the stage to show off Nvidia's new hardware are now over.

What's next for Huang? Only he knows, but he'll likely retire with a pretty substantial golden handshake. As the largest shareholder in Nvidia--a company currently valued at trillions --Jensen's stock is also worth billions if he ever decides to sell.

news.title: GTA 4 的三叶草抢劫案展示了如何不抢银行——关卡艺术
news.summary: This is how Michael Mann’s Heat inspired GTA 4’s legendary Three Leaf Clover mission, shaping Rockstar’s reali

content.v: https://assets-prd.ignimgs.com/2026/11/11/blog-1794413799371.jpg

Ask a dozen average punters what the best mission in GTA 5 is, and you’ll get several dozen answers. Ask the same box of eggs about Grand Theft Auto 4 and a consensus will emerge: it's Three Leaf Clover . A bickering bank-heist that starts on the border of outright slapstick but quickly turns into a masterclass of escalating tension, where the streets of Liberty City become a Pac-Man maze of hot flying lead in yet another glorious Grand Theft Homage to the works of filmmaker Michael Mann. It’s the crowning achievement of an otherwise very divisive game.

GTA 4 remains the most curious beast in Rockstar’s blockbuster menagerie: a brand new start in an era of unprecedented sophistication and visual fidelity, with the ever-capable hardware of the time leveraged into depicting the cold forever-autumn of Liberty City: a suitable backdrop for the grubby, boldly bleak tale of a man on the run from his past, a story chiefly about disillusionment, of treacheries within and without. A far cry from the endless summers of Vice City and San Andreas. If California knows how to party, New York City knows how to freeze your bollocks off on a park bench.

GTA 4 was in the same breath a huge step forward for Rockstar’s world-building and storytelling chops, while also being a deliberate back-to-basics reset for their flagship series. Structurally, it’s a lot closer to the original GTA and GTA 3 than its immediate predecessor, San Andreas , and it’s even less sophisticated than Vice City in key areas. GTA 4 has no real estate sub-game. Niko cannot gain weight by stuffing his face, or get jacked by lifting stuff. GTA 4’s missions tend to be short, sharp, shooty-bang vignettes where the player only has to work against the game’s chief objects of friction: angry NPCs with guns, and the unforgiving driving model that makes your average canalboat-sized American sedan handle like a bouncy castle on swampland.

In short, it’s brilliant. But it does leave us with only one real answer when it comes to its best or most iconic mission, and that’s when you tag along with the Irish mob for a hastily undertaken bank heist in Chinatown.

Though Three Leaf Clover is credited by Rockstar itself for inspiring the intricately designed heists of GTA 5 and GTA Online — as well as the lauded three-protagonist mechanic allowing players to switch between Michael, Franklin, and Trevor at key moments — Three Leaf Clover itself barely hints at such complexities. If anything, it’s the complete antithesis of a GTA 5 heist: there’s no planning involved, save for the almost arbitrary requirement to go buy a suit and tie and a hasty en-route briefing from Patrick McCreary.

Unsurprisingly given the lack of prep, things go wrong from the off. While Patrick and Derrick are arguing about how to treat the hostages, one of them, an idiotic NRA member, decides to be today's "good guy with a gun". Michael Keane, not Batman’s butler, cops it when Eugene Reaper unconceals his carry. For the final time, as it turns out, when Patrick and Derrick shoot him to death in revenge. Luis Lopez, the tertiary protagonist of the GTA 4 saga and star of the Ballad of Gay Tony DLC, keeps his head down sensibly, although the player can choose to kill him if they enjoy messing with the space-time continuum.

The vault is blown with probably too much C4, a cool million dollars gets shoved into duffel bags, and all hell breaks loose on the streets: the bank is descended upon by scores of LCPD. Hundreds of cops and dozens of patrol cars block every escape route, turning the streets into killing corridors. Cover is scarce and flimsy: Niko can peek around corners, duck behind bins, or use parked cars as makeshift shield walls. Unfortunately, in hails of gunfire, cars are liable to explode, due to this being an era when people could afford to put gas in them.

The cavernous tenements and skyscrapers echo with barrages of bullets. Footsteps bounce around the walls as the crew dives into a subway station in a desperate attempt to get out of the open. The player somehow hears all this over the thumping of their own heart. If Niko dies, it’s back to Patrick’s mum’s house for a restart. If either of your companions die, it’s over. Kill too many civilians? Also a fail state. Lose the money? Fail. Car blows up? Fail. Abandon your crew? Fail. There are no mid-mission checkpoints: Three Leaf Clover is a mission that requires as much luck as skill to clear. It’s not an especially hard mission, but it’s easy to have a bad time with it through no fault of your own. Conversely, it’s perfectly possible to stumble through it with dumb luck. You need good fortune to make a fortune. As with all GTA missions, the game’s open world systems can work with or against you.

And this is a huge part of why it’s so tense. If you’ve been unlucky in your first attempt, the stakes get higher with every subsequent run: this is a crucial story mission that unlocks the last third of the entire map. But aside from the consequences of failure, Three Leaf Clover’s sheer lack of bells and whistles gives the whole experience an air of deadly realism that cuts through GTA’s baseline silliness by stripping it back to its most basic elements. Shooting. Running. Driving. Cops and robbers. Borrowing heavily once again from the works of filmmaker Michael Mann, most obviously 1995’s Heat, Three Leaf Clover refuses the temptation to underscore its action with the appropriate musical accompaniment, instead painting a symphony of death with strictly diegetic audio. No needle drops. No radios to bark crisply with the dialogue of your colleagues, no matter how far away they are. The sound is raw, real, unsweetened. Or, at least, it’s painstakingly designed to seem that way, and so successfully that you’re liable to forget that these are all sounds being triggered by clever scripting and a sophisticated real-time engine.

It’s this approach to sound design that really hammers home how much the people behind GTA are in love with Mann’s filmography, to the point where Grand Theft Auto is probably the most significant cultural force keeping the relevance of Miami Vice alive. Vice City and the upcoming GTA 6 are obviously massively indebted to what was one of the greatest TV shows of the 1980s, a rare example of one that still absolutely holds up today. The juxtaposition of pina coladas, speedboats, and sharp suits against a seedy criminal drug trade fuelling gang violence and urban decline certainly must have appealed to the Houser brothers and many of their collaborators, given how much of their stock in trade is based on those exact vibes. And it’s not hard to imagine why even the tainted glamour of a crime-ridden Miami would seem like paradise to kids growing up in 1980s Britain, purely by virtue of the fact that everything didn’t look like it was covered in a thin film of shit.

Miami Vice is just one side of the coin when it comes to Michael Mann’s influence on GTA: much is made of how Three Leaf Clover is directly inspired by the brilliant bank heist in Heat, right down to the outfits, which explains why Patrick McCreary is so insistent on Niko looking the part before the mission can even start. Three Leaf Clover plays out markedly differently to the Heat heist, with the inherent claustrophobia of Liberty City’s labyrinthine streets and alleys feeling a lot less exposed than the wide thoroughfares of downtown LA. But anyone who watches Heat for the first time will be struck by how minimalist the score is for such a high-stakes action thriller.

news.title: XBOX CEO发布致全员信
news.summary: 游戏行业的生产关系，“正在被打破” 太平洋时间11 月 12 日上午 ，XBOX Wire 公开了 CEO Asha Sharma 以《 XBOX 25 周年》为题，发给XBOX全球员工的一封信。 在信中，Asha回顾了

content.v: 游戏行业的生产关系，“正在被打破”
太平洋时间11 月 12 日上午 ，XBOX Wire 公开了 CEO Asha Sharma 以《 XBOX 25 周年》为题，发给XBOX全球员工的一封信。
在信中，Asha回顾了微软如何从早期的《微软大冒险》和《微软模拟飞行》涉足游戏行业，再到 2001 年推出初代 XBOX，以及发展到今天的历程。
她在信中确认第五代主机“即将到来”，并提到“纵观人类历史，我们的创造规模由人力、资金与资源决定。而这种关系正在被打破。未来，一个人将能掌握海量的才能与能力；一个小团队就可以打造如今需数百人和数亿美元才能完成的世界；而更大型的工作室则能追求超越当下的游戏梦想”。
这或许预示着在 AI 等开发工具快速演进的背景下，XBOX面向游戏行业未来发展所做的判断，以及将进一步作出的调整。
以下为此次全员信完整原文：
XBOX 25 周年
https://alioss.yystv.cn/doc/14619/2360af1b02fe2fd61a994d53aafd1071.jpeg_mw680water
各位团队成员：
微软成立初衷是相信现代计算能够让普通人拥有非凡的能力。而自公司创立以来，游戏就一直是这段故事中的一部分。
1979 年，我们推出了文字冒险游戏《微软大冒险》（Microsoft Adventure）。这款游戏的画面类似 MS-DOS，不同于早期版本的《我的世界》。它由微软最初 13 名员工中一位名叫 Gordon Letwin 的开发者改编，他后来成为了 OS/2 的架构师。这款游戏让玩家能够探索数字世界、收集宝藏、解谜，偶遇神话生物。
https://alioss.yystv.cn/doc/14619/eaa5376459be8e4db7f06562069e105a.jpeg_mw680water
数年后，Bruce Artwick 把飞行的魔力带到了 16 位 IBM PC上，让人们可以在办公桌前驾驶飞机。在随后的十年里，微软又发布了几十款游戏，包括《扫雷》、《帝国时代》和另外 4 个版本的《微软模拟飞行》，同时 Windows 也与 id Software 等合作伙伴一起推动了 3D 游戏的兴起（后者也在 24 年后加入了 XBOX 大家庭）。
https://alioss.yystv.cn/doc/14619/b2e4bb0c4f0c7515d42cc29957fb72c7.jpeg_mw680water
来到 90 年代中期，一个负责 DirectX 的小团队提出了一个大胆的想法，他们认为我们可以用 PC 架构来打造首台美式游戏主机（DirectX 是一项帮助开发者为 Windows 编写游戏的技术），于是不久后，一个名为“Project Midway”的秘密项目启动了。
2001 年，初代 XBOX 闪亮登场。它比竞争对手的主机大两到三倍，外壳上印有巨大的 X 标志，中央镶嵌着亮绿色的徽章。在竞争对手还在要求玩家单独购买存储卡的时候，它就配备了硬盘，并配有以太网接口，这在当时十分罕见，因为当时 9 成家庭仍在使用拨号上网。它的处理性能是当时同类竞争对手的两倍以上，同时开创了双摇杆控制器的先河。
一年后，XBOX Live 改变了在线游戏的格局，它引入了持久好友列表、匹配系统以及供开发者构建联网体验的统一服务。而汇聚这些创新的，是《光环：战斗进化》——这款首发游戏不仅定义了 XBOX，也印证了它的首个广告语：“游戏，从此不同。”
https://alioss.yystv.cn/doc/14619/5f454216ec718a5420889d076dbf8c24.jpeg_mw680water

25 年后的今天，XBOX 已发展成为全球最大的游戏公司之一。我们推出了 4 个世代的 XBOX 主机，同时第五代也即将到来。如今，我们的游戏每年触达超过十亿玩家，涵盖了《使命召唤》、《糖果传奇》、《暗黑破坏神》、《毁灭战士》、《神鬼寓言》、《辐射》、《极限竞速》、《战争机器》、《光环》、《我的世界》、《守望先锋》、《盗贼之海》、《上古卷轴》、《星际争霸》、《魔兽世界》、《德军总部》等在内的众多标志性系列。
致所有创造了 XBOX 的人们
XBOX 的故事由一代又一代的员工、工作室、开发者和合作伙伴共同书写。感谢你们所有人。同时，我也要在此特别向 111 位在 XBOX 及旗下工作室中服务了超 25 年的同事致敬。你们帮助塑造了我们今日所庆祝的历史，我们将为你们每人赠送一台特别定制并刻有铭文的主机，以纪念你们的贡献。
自从我加入 XBOX 以来，我听到了许多令人动容的故事：我听到有人因一次联机结识，并成为终生挚友；有人在游戏中结识了自己的另一半；还有父母与孩子一起重温他们儿时玩的游戏。我也听说过那些已经离开我们的人，以及他们留下的游戏回忆对亲友仍然意义深远。这就是我们存在的理由。
XBOX 的故事，从来不只属于我们自己。我们的粉丝激励我们、支持我们、督促我们，并与我们一路相伴。一路以来，我们与全球玩家共同庆祝这个纪念日，推出了各种特别活动。今天，这场庆典将在西雅图迎来高潮。
下一个 25 年
游戏产业始终由梦想推动。不仅是把想象的世界变为现实，更是与他人分享。有时梦想是一款游戏，有时是一台主机、一个角色，或一个完整的宇宙。XBOX 的历史证明了这些梦想的力量，以及它们如何随着时间成长。
初代《微软模拟飞行》仅有 160KB 大小，2D 图形、16 种颜色、共 20 个机场。而 2024 版则调用了超过 2.5PB 的数据，比初代作品大了 150 亿倍，地图面积达到 2 亿平方英里，几乎重现了地球上的每一座城市、每一条道路和地标，渲染了数万亿棵树，并实现了近乎实时的真实天气。
尽管现代游戏在创造力和技术上已经达到了几乎难以想象的高度，但它们的开发成本、资源与风险也同样猛增。结果是，太多想法未能成为游戏，太多游戏未能实现开发者的初衷。几十年来，这是雄心与现实之间无可避免的取舍。我们必须改变这一点。
纵观人类历史，我们的创造规模由人力、资金与资源决定。而这种关系正在被打破。未来，一个人将能掌握海量的才能与能力；一个小团队就可以打造如今需数百人和数亿美元才能完成的世界；而更大型的工作室则能追求超越当下的游戏梦想，就像《微软模拟飞行 2024》之于 1982 年版所实现的跨越。
我相信未来的游戏将重回它的起点，回到那个一个小团队凭一个伟大的创意，就能创造改变游戏世界玩法的时刻。我们的使命，就是持续打造卓越的游戏、鲜明的硬件，并让更多人有机会创造前所未见的作品。
生日快乐，XBOX！
Asha

news.title: 《GTA6》评级细节曝光！男主裸露画面或不在正式版
news.summary: 据外媒TheGamer报道，韩国曾一度险些拒绝为《GTA6》进行评级，原因是游戏中出现了大量缺乏情境铺垫的裸露画面。

content.v: 据外媒TheGamer报道，韩国曾一度险些拒绝为《GTA6》进行评级，原因是游戏中出现了大量缺乏情境铺垫的裸露画面。
该作在多个地区都获得了最高级别的成人评级。不过，韩国方面的评级过程却并不顺利。据报道，韩国评级机构曾一度考虑拒绝为游戏评级，其中一个重要原因就是游戏中存在“角色私密部位裸露”的画面。
https://img1.gamersky.com/upimg/pic/2026/11/12/small_202611122322375875.jpg
一名评级委员会成员指出，此类裸露画面之所以成为问题，是因为过去从未有游戏如此频繁地呈现缺乏情境铺垫或“叙事合理性”的裸体内容。韩国评级委员会首次召开会议时，最终以平票收场。随后，委员会要求提供游戏副本，以进一步评估其中的“表现”。
在审查过程中，委员会发现，游戏中的“裸露场景”大多是独立出现于背景中的画面，并不会引发后续互动。此前黑客大葱哥Cyberleek泄露的裸体主义者聚会场景也成为审查重点，委员会甚至多次要求Take-Two提供游戏地图，以便找到这一场景。
https://img1.gamersky.com/upimg/pic/2026/11/12/small_202611122322303113.jpg
最终，韩国方面还是决定为《GTA6》颁发成人专属评级（Adults Only）。这一决定在一定程度上也与此前Cyberleek裸露画面泄露事件有关。评级人员在正式游戏中并未发现这些泄露画面，外媒认为，这也进一步确认，此前相关内容来自开发版本遭到黑客入侵，并非游戏原本计划呈现的正式内容。
目前尚不清楚Rockstar或Take-Two是否为通过评级而对游戏进行了任何修改，但至少《GTA6》最终还是获得了韩国方面的正式评级。

content.v: 由你来说： 黄仁勋执掌英伟达33年，将公司带上全球AI芯片巨头的地位，却也因个人丑闻引发巨大争议。你认为这些争议会影响你对他的评价吗？他的离开又会给英伟达和游戏玩家带来怎样的变化？
11月12日，英伟达官方发布公告，宣布公司联合创始人黄仁勋已辞去总裁、首席执行官（CEO）及董事会成员职务。公司现任执行副总裁兼首席财务官科莱特·克雷斯（Colette Kress）将出任临时CEO，直至正式继任者确定。
消息公布后，相关话题迅速登上微博和推特热搜，引发广泛关注。
https://img1.gamersky.com/upimg/pic/2026/11/12/small_202611122300462092.png
https://img1.gamersky.com/upimg/pic/2026/11/12/small_202611122300469262.png
黄仁勋是英伟达联合创始人，自1993年公司成立以来一直担任领导职务，执掌公司长达33年。在他的带领下，英伟达从一家图形芯片厂商逐步发展为全球AI芯片巨头。
此次人事变动发生在黄仁勋个人丑闻持续发酵之际。此前，黄仁勋承认对妻子不忠，并就自己的行为向家人及公司员工道歉。与此同时，媒体还报道称，他曾与一名女商人以及公司内部一名高管存在婚外关系。不过，英伟达董事会发布的辞职公告并未明确说明黄仁勋离职的具体原因。
消息传出后，玩家社区也展开了热烈讨论。有玩家调侃，黄仁勋卸任后，显卡价格是不是终于有望降下来了？
https://img1.gamersky.com/upimg/pic/2026/11/12/small_202611122301065528.png
还有人将此次事件与黄仁勋此前强调英伟达是“AI基础设施公司”，而非游戏公司的言论联系起来，认为他近年来将重心转向AI、忽视了游戏玩家，如今的处境多少有些讽刺。
当然，也有不少网友对他的离开表示惋惜。部分玩家认为，黄仁勋在CUDA、RTX以及AI芯片领域作出的贡献不容忽视，个人丑闻不应完全抹杀他过去30多年来对科技行业的影响。另一些人则担忧，此次高层变动可能影响英伟达未来的发展方向、公司股价乃至整个AI行业。
此外，还有玩家感叹，“皮夹克时代”或许就此落幕，以后再也看不到黄仁勋穿着标志性的皮夹克，在发布会上亲自公布新一代显卡了。
https://img1.gamersky.com/upimg/pic/2026/11/12/small_202611122301238425.png
当然，社区里也不乏调侃声音。有人拿他的婚外情事件开玩笑，称他辞职后终于有时间陪伴“女朋友们”；也有人调侃，与其关注公司的未来，不如先准备迎接《GTA6》。

news.title: 英伟达市值蒸发4万亿元！黄仁勋辞职影响巨大
news.summary: 受灵魂人物黄仁勋突发辞任公司总裁、CEO及董事职务的重磅人事巨震影响，美股芯片巨头英伟达引发了资本市场的剧烈恐慌。

content.v: 受灵魂人物黄仁勋突发辞任公司总裁、CEO及董事职务的重磅人事巨震影响，美股芯片巨头英伟达引发了资本市场的剧烈恐慌。
https://img1.gamersky.com/upimg/pic/2026/11/12/small_202611122258238103.jpg
北京时间12日晚间，英伟达盘初重挫超14%，最低触及148.8美元，创去年6月以来新低，较10月6日创下的历史高点(243.37美元)跌去近40%。盘中市值蒸发超6000亿美元（约合4万亿元人民币），最新市值约3.6万亿美元，跌至美股第三位。截至发稿，英伟达跌幅收窄至6%。
这场史诗级的抛售，直接反映了华尔街对失去“皮衣老黄”这一核心领军人物后，英伟达在AI芯片领域能否继续保持绝对统治力的深度担忧。

news.title: 花费数千美元购买人工智能工具的神奇宝贝粉丝对 Anthropic 终于开始打压感到不满
news.summary: A Pokémon fan who claimed to be spending thousands of dollars each month building a vibe-coded AI project is n

content.v: https://assets-prd.ignimgs.com/2026/11/12/untitled-1-1794495208363.jpg
A Pokémon fan who claimed to be spending thousands of dollars each month building a vibe-coded AI project is now complaining after Claude AI maker Anthropic finally introduced copyright limitations.

Claude models are now "starting to refuse" to work on projects that include official Pokémon assets, according to Pocket Monster fan Big Kid Nation. In a post on X/Twitter last night, Big Kid Nation went on to lament the fact that no money had ever been made on the project despite significant investment, unlike other similar projects that are being funded through Patreon.

"Anthropic has cracked down and Claude models are starting to refuse work on Pokémon fan projects," Big Kid Nation wrote , attaching a screenshot in which Claude stated it could no longer generate code designed to work with images it detected as featuring official Pokémon designs.

"All that money spent, never took a cent (unlike many others with itch.io, Patreon etc.)," Big Kid Nation continued. "Nintendo. Just make the epic Pokémon game you know we all want. I'll live on the street and work for free if it helps."

Big Kid Nation is currently building "Pokémon Arena 2D," a game that has somehow escaped the beady eyes of The Pokémon Company's lawyers up to this point, but seems unlikely to do so for much longer. "Real-time arena battles in pixel art," reads a description listed on BigKidNation.com. "Two years in the making, and free to play."

In another X/Twitter post made earlier this month, Big Kid Nation claimed they were racking up as much as "$2,000 expenses a month and 10-14 hour days both learning and building for most of this year and last." And while the game was coded using AI tools, Big Kid Nation was keen to push back on those branding it simply as "AI slop."
Big Kid Nation said that they set their PC running overnight simulating battles within Pokémon Arena 2D to try and detect balance issues, and then spent 14 hours a day sitting at the computer itself.

"Vibe coding games is so fun," Big Kid Nation wrote in another post , made last month. "There are some negatives with unethical vibe coders. But you're creative and love game development it's just a dream. What took me a year to make people can make in a week. And some can't make anything original. But those with ideas it's just one thing after another."

As an example of another "original vibe coded project", Big Kid Nation pointed to the separately-developed Poké Derby, which appears to be a Pokémon-themed version of the hugely popular Japanese racehorse game Umamusume. "This is what I'm talking about," Big Kid Nation wrote. "Instead of seeing ideas and just taking them with no creativity, these guys just build their own unique world from scratch."
Numerous comments on this post pointed out the fact this was in fact a Pokémon-themed version of Umamusume, seemingly to no avail.
The next official Pokémon games to release remain Pokémon Winds and Waves , which will arrive exclusively for Nintendo Switch 2 next year. Maybe it's best to just wait for those?

news.title: 《马里奥赛车世界》Switch 2 黑色星期五特惠让价格回到 2025 年水平
news.summary: Nintendo has announced its 2026 Black Friday deals, with a Mario Kart World Switch 2 hardware bundle as the ce

content.v: Nintendo has announced its 2026 Black Friday deals, with a Mario Kart World Switch 2 hardware bundle as the centerpiece for $500.

The Switch 2 launched in 2025 with a similar bundle for the same price, but it was discontinued at the end of the year. It later returned , but at a higher price point--$550. Now, the bundle is on "sale" again, though it's the same price as it was in 2025 before the price hikes. In addition to a digital copy of the game and the console, it comes with a three-month Nintendo Switch Online membership.
https://www.gamespot.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/11/Switch2bundle.jpg?w=636

The bundle goes on sale November 22 and will be available through December 5. It's not the only hardware bundle that people can buy, as Nintendo also offers a system with a digital copy of Nintendo Switch Sports Resort and three months of Switch Online for $530. This bundle is not on sale for Black Friday, though.
Get the Mario Kart World Switch 2 hardware bundle here:
Additionally, for just one week--November 22-29--Nintendo will offer games like Donkey Kong Bananza and Super Mario Galaxy + Super Mario Galaxy 2 for $20 off.
What's more, Nintendo announced that the Nintendo eShop and the Nintendo Store will offer a range of deals November 19-December 2, but it hasn’t yet detailed what you can expect.

Black Friday used to be just one day of deals--the day after Thanksgiving in the US--but now it's an entire season of savings. Keep checking back with GameSpot for more Black Friday deals in the days ahead.

news.title: 《怪猎：旅人》IGN7分！核心玩法强大但惨遭拖累
news.summary: IGN发布了对《怪物猎人：旅人》的评测文章，给出了7分的评价。

content.v: IGN发布了对《怪物猎人：旅人》的评测文章，给出了7分的评价。
简评： 《怪物猎人：旅人》巧妙地将该系列狂热的战斗模式适配到了移动端，但其强大的核心玩法却被玩家再熟悉不过的抽卡机制和无休止的菜单所拖累。
评分 7 分
https://img1.gamersky.com/upimg/pic/2026/11/12/small_202611122245545693.png
https://img1.gamersky.com/upimg/pic/2026/11/12/small_202611122244226927.jpg

总评： 《怪物猎人：旅人》就是那种塞了太多东西的游戏；它充斥着各种需要去费心管理的移动端式冗余内容，其中很大一部分妨碍了玩家去享受它本身明显具备的强大玩法。在许多方面，《旅人》的野心之大确实令人惊叹，它如此巧妙地将《怪物猎人：世界》的精彩之处整合进了一个体量更小的平台中。对战斗系统的巧妙精简依然保留了狩猎的紧张激烈感，同时让游戏更适合利用碎片时间游玩。虽然游戏里有足够多的优点能让你保持投入，但它也同样伴随着诸多令人沮丧的痛点，比如收费机制、进度卡点，以及无休止的菜单管理带来的烦恼。这意味着，归根结底，《旅人》未能企及其主机版本的高度，但如果你能带着降低后的预期去游玩，怪物猎人的核心灵魂依然存在。

news.title: 《GTA6》地图海报实物完整版曝光！大量地标展示
news.summary: 近日，有爆料人在网络上公开了《GTA 6》收藏版中附带的实体地图。

content.v: 近日，有爆料人在网络上公开了《GTA 6》收藏版中附带的实体地图。
玩家们可以通过这张地图，清晰地看到游戏虚拟州“雷奥尼达”（Leonida）的庞大版图以及多个关键地标节点。
不过需要注意的是，这张曝光的实体地图并非十分详尽的1:1游戏内地图，而是一张标有关键地标的概览海报。
https://img1.gamersky.com/upimg/pic/2026/11/12/small_202611122237268767.jpg
从图片中可以看出，整个地图被设计成了充满复古与漫画风格的观光地图，不仅展示了地形，还印有大量极具佛罗里达特色的趣味插画，如飞艇、火烈鸟、重装皮卡、比基尼女郎、甚至UFO和沼泽怪物。
根据地图上的文字信息，我们可以梳理出以下关键节点：
主要行政区划（郡县）：
Lummox County（位于右上角区域）
Kelly County（位于左上角区域）
Leonard County（位于右侧，包含巨大的Lake Leonida湖泊）
Vice Dale County（位于中下部，核心城市Vice City罪恶都市所在地）
Mariana County（位于左下角，包含沼泽区域）
核心城市与主要地标：
Vice City（罪恶都市）：地图右侧的核心大都市，高楼林立。
K.C. City：位于地图中下方，标志性插画是一个UFO。
Port Gellhorn：左上角的沿海港口城市。
Grassrivers：左下角的沼泽地带。
其他特色区域及岛屿：
群岛：地图四周散布着多个岛屿，包括顶部的Featherstone Islands、左上的Zephyr Islands、右上的Stamford Islands，以及右下角的Gloriana Key、Catalan Key和Corsair Key等。
街区/区域：包括Ambrosia、Emerald Springs、Buckskin Swamp、Little Cuba、Southside以及Pelican Valley等。
交通网络：地图上清晰标注了多条公路编号（如404、183、35、97等），右下角还有明显的“Toll”（收费站）标志。
